summary: H.J. Res. 130 is a joint resolution that nullifies a Bureau of Land Management rule from November 2024. That rule had amended the 2015 resource management plan for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming to make no federal coal available for future leasing. By nullifying the rule, this legislation requires the Bureau of Land Management to follow the 2015 plan instead, thereby making federal coal resources in that planning area available for future leasing again.

affected_groups.effect: Must disregard the 2024 resource management plan amendment and follow the 2015 resource management plan instead, making coal available for leasing.
Gain the opportunity for future federal coal leasing since coal resources are made available again.
affected_groups.group: Entities interested in federal coal leasing in the Buffalo Field Office planning area

key_provisions: Disapproves and nullifies the Bureau of Land Management rule titled Buffalo Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment issued on November 20, 2024.
States that the nullified rule shall have no force or effect.
Requires the Bureau of Land Management to follow the 2015 resource management plan as it existed before the 2024 amendment.
Makes federal coal resources in the Buffalo Field Office planning area available for future leasing.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.J. Res. 130 is a joint resolution that nullifies a Bureau of Land Management rule from November 2024. That rule had amended the 2015 resource management plan for the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming to make no federal coal available for future leasing. By nullifying the rule, this legislation requires the Bureau of Land Management to follow the 2015 plan instead, thereby making federal coal resources in that planning area available for future leasing again.
summary_detail.significance: The joint resolution reverses a specific federal administrative decision that had stopped future federal coal leasing in a specific Wyoming field office, returning land management policy back to the 2015 framework.
